decisions.reason: As a fairly generic address-autocomplete web service outside the firm's main regulated-energy specialization, it is more likely to be discontinued or folded into broader solutions than kept as a standalone product.
A grid-fee database fits the firm's core strengths in regulated market data and compliance support, even if the Austrian niche makes it somewhat more vulnerable than domestic core products.
This service is closely aligned with the firm's analytical and regulatory-process offering and supports its move toward modular, process-based digital services.
An end-customer tariff database is strongly consistent with the firm's long-built data assets and platform direction, and the multi-model line suggests enough breadth to justify retention.
Custom web services are less scalable and less aligned with the firm's stated shift toward standardized SaaS modules and end-to-end platform offerings.
A postal-code lookup service is highly commoditized and peripheral to the firm's differentiated energy-market expertise, making discontinuation relatively likely.
